research_question: In adults undergoing surgery for symptomatic haemorrhoids, does LigaSure (vessel-sealing device) haemorrhoidectomy reduce operating time (minutes) compared with conventional excisional haemorrhoidectomy (scissors, diathermy/electrocautery, Milligan-Morgan or Ferguson technique)?
control_label: Conventional excisional haemorrhoidectomy (scissors, diathermy/electrocautery, Milligan-Morgan or Ferguson)
outcome_description: Operating time in minutes, measured as duration of the haemorrhoidectomy procedure (e.g. from incision/start of excision to completion of the operation), reported as mean (SD) per arm or convertible statistics (median/IQR/range, SE, 95% CI, t or F values).
positive_direction: A positive effect indicates that LigaSure haemorrhoidectomy results in a SHORTER operating time than conventional haemorrhoidectomy (i.e. favours LigaSure; equivalent to a raw mean difference below zero in minutes).
search_queries: LigaSure haemorrhoidectomy randomized trial operating time
vessel sealing device hemorrhoidectomy versus conventional Milligan-Morgan comparison
LigaSure versus diathermy hemorrhoidectomy operative time outcomes
inclusion_criteria: Studies of adults undergoing haemorrhoidectomy for symptomatic haemorrhoids (any grade) in which a LigaSure or similar vessel-sealing device technique is compared with a conventional excisional technique (scissors, diathermy/electrocautery, Milligan-Morgan, Ferguson or similar)
Any comparative design (randomised controlled trial, quasi-experimental, prospective or retrospective comparative cohort) reporting at least one quantitative outcome
Reports operating/operative time or other quantitative perioperative outcome data in a form allowing effect-size computation (means and SDs, medians with spread, t/F statistics, or proportions)
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, narrative reviews, editorials, letters, opinion pieces, case reports, theoretical or technique-description papers without data)
No comparison between a LigaSure/vessel-sealing treatment group and a conventional haemorrhoidectomy control group (single-arm or non-comparative studies)
No extractable quantitative outcome data to produce an effect size (no means+SDs, t/F values, proportions, odds ratios or convertible statistics)

Completely unrelated to the research topic (e.g. vessel-sealing devices used in non-haemorrhoid surgery, or haemorrhoid treatments such as stapled haemorrhoidopexy or rubber band ligation with no conventional-excision comparison)
moderators_to_extract: Type of conventional comparator (scissors/cold steel, diathermy, Milligan-Morgan, Ferguson)
Anaesthesia type and day-case vs inpatient setting
effect_size_note: Pool as a raw mean difference (MD) in minutes with a random-effects (DerSimonian-Laird/REML) model; MD < 0 favours LigaSure (shorter operation). Where only medians with IQR/range are reported, convert to mean and SD using standard methods (Wan et al. / Luo et al.). Assess heterogeneity with I-squared and tau-squared and inspect funnel plot/Egger's test if >=10 studies.
